object_description: two staggered building volumes linked by an upper walkway
design_condition: Two differently sized buildings combine both construction sites, respond to the residential and track-field edges through staggered setbacks, and create a viaduct-facing address space with a lowered entrance level connected to the underpass and city stream.

positive.statement: The urban-planning setting creates well-proportioned outdoor spaces and clear addressing.
The building complex and open-space design form a clear and memorable whole.
The main hall offers a clear, spacious, and exciting spatial experience.
The large building's access routes and platforms bring identity to the central space.
The wooden structure and upper-floor grid are cleverly chosen for the respective requirements.
The floor plans offer extremely good flexibility for room changes.
The roof and facade are used for electricity production.

negative.statement: The internal access via a serpentine ramp is unfavorable.
The required playing field and east-west connection along the city stream are not proven.
The building expression does not correspond to the intended use of the university.
The smaller building's foyer is too small for the three public halls.
The many long corridors with little daylight are narrow.
The use groups are neither clearly separated nor logically adjacent.
All small lecture halls and some required operating procedures are missing.
The large room depths on the lower floors result in insufficient daylight conditions.
